claims.text: Tungsten and molybdenum are high-melting-point transition metals.
Adding 1–5 atomic percent tungsten or molybdenum to a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding 1–5 atomic percent tungsten or molybdenum will improve the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
The added high-melting-point transition-metal atoms can act as network formers or network disruptors.
The added transition metal will increase atomic packing density.
The added transition metal will hinder crystallization.
The added transition metal will introduce atomic-size mismatch.
The added transition metal will produce strong chemical interactions in the alloy.
Atomic-size mismatch and strong chemical interactions will increase the energy barrier for crystallization.
The increased crystallization barrier will suppress nucleation and growth of crystalline phases.
The modified alloy will require a lower critical cooling rate for amorphization than the otherwise comparable alloy without the addition.
The modified alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature in DSC than the otherwise comparable alloy without the addition.
The intervention may fail if the added transition metal forms intermetallic compounds.
The intervention may fail if the initial alloy composition is already optimized for glass formation and amorphous-state thermal stability.
